sources.entry: Buku - Powerful bookmark manager and a personal textual mini-web. GPL-3.0 Python/deb

summary.one_liner: buku is a command-line bookmark manager (Python) that stores bookmarks in a private, portable database and works as a personal text-based mini-web.
summary.what_it_does: buku stores bookmarks with auto-fetched titles, tags and descriptions, and can import bookmarks from Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, Vivaldi, Brave and MS Edge or from HTML, XBEL, JSON, Markdown, Org, RSS/Atom and buku .db files. Search supports ANY/ALL keyword modes, regex, substring (deep) matching, field markers for title, URL, description and tags, and tag-based search with include and exclude logic. Export goes to HTML, XBEL, Markdown, Org, RSS/Atom or a buku database. It can check broken links against the Wayback Machine, open bookmarks in a browser, and encrypt the database with a lock/unlock command. The README also mentions bukuserver as a separate browsable web front-end and a library interface with related projects such as a browser plug-in.
use_cases: manage bookmarks from the command line
import browser bookmarks into one portable database
search saved links by keyword, regex or tag
export bookmarks to HTML, Markdown, Org or XBEL
find cached copies of dead links on the Wayback Machine
keep bookmarks organized with tags and comments
how_to_run: apt-get install ca-certificates python3-urllib3 python3-cryptography python3-bs4
stack: Bash, Fish and Zsh completion scripts
notable: Imports directly from multiple major browsers and several bookmark file formats
Search with markers to target title, URL, description or tags separately
Tag management with redirection operators (>>, >) at the prompt
Wayback Machine lookup for broken links
Database can be merged and synced between systems
caveats: Command-line tool; the GUI is a separate project (bukuserver) described only by reference
CentOS may lack the python3-beautifulsoup4 package and need pip3 install
Release packages cover only the CLI component
